questions.stem: In an **Inelastic collision**:

options.B: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
options.D: Neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved.

explanation_steps:
In an **inelastic collision**, the objects may stick together or deform. 
- **Momentum** is always conserved in any isolated collision.
- **Kinetic Energy** is NOT conserved; some of it is converted into heat, sound, or internal energy.

questions.stem: If a ball is swinging in a circle on a string and moved twice as fast, the force on the string will be:
explanation_steps:
The force on the string is the **centripetal force**: 
$$ F = \frac{mv^2}{r} $$
If velocity ($$ v $$) is doubled ($$ 2v $$):
$$ F_{new} = \frac{m(2v)^2}{r} = \frac{4mv^2}{r} = 4F_{original} $$
The force becomes four times as great.

questions.stem: A spring has an original length of $$ 100 \text{ cm} $$. After adding a mass of $$ 400 \text{ kg} $$, the spring will be $$ 200 \text{ cm} $$ long. Its spring constant in $$ N/m $$ is:
explanation_steps:

$$ F = mg = 400 \text{ kg} \times 10 \text{ m/s}^2 = 4000 \text{ N} $$

**Step 2: Calculate the extension ($$ x $$) in meters.**
$$ x = L_{final} - L_{initial} = 200 \text{ cm} - 100 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ cm} = 1 \text{ m} $$

questions.stem: If we convert $$ 100^\circ\text{C} $$ to temperature Kelvin and temperature Fahrenheit it gives respectively:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert to Kelvin.**
$$ K = C + 273 = 100 + 273 = 373 \text{ K} $$

**Step 2: Convert to Fahrenheit.**
$$ F = (C \times 1.8) + 32 = (100 \times 1.8) + 32 = 180 + 32 = 212^\circ\text{F} $$

Result: 373 & 212.

questions.stem: Object A has $$ 150 \text{ kg} $$ mass and object B has $$ 200 \text{ kg} $$ mass. Which object has **smallest inertia**?
explanation_steps:
**Inertia** is the resistance of an object to change its state of motion. It is directly proportional to **mass**. 
- Less mass = Less inertia.
- Object A ($$ 150 \text{ kg} $$) has less mass than Object B ($$ 200 \text{ kg} $$), so Object A has the smallest inertia.

questions.stem: The complementary colour of Red colour is:
explanation_steps:
**Complementary colors** are pairs of colors which, when combined, produce white light. 
- Red + **Cyan** = White.
- Green + Magenta = White.
- Blue + Yellow = White.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is **not** the property of electric charge?

options.D: Electric charges can be positive or negative.

explanation_steps: An **electroscope** (such as a gold-leaf electroscope) is used to detect the presence and magnitude of electric charge on a body through the repulsion of like-charged metal leaves.

explanation_steps: A **multimeter** (also known as a VOM or AVO meter) is an electronic measuring instrument that combines several measurement functions in one unit, typically including voltage, current, and resistance.

questions.stem: Hypermetropia (long sight) is corrected by ________________.
explanation_steps: **Hypermetropia** occurs when the eyeball is too short or the lens is too thin, causing light to focus behind the retina. A **convex lens** converges light rays before they enter the eye, moving the focus point forward onto the retina.

questions.stem: A ____________ is a device used to increase or decrease AC voltage.
explanation_steps: A **transformer** works on the principle of mutual induction. It consists of primary and secondary coils. It can be 'step-up' (increases voltage) or 'step-down' (decreases voltage).

questions.stem: ______________ is a single vector that is equal to the sum of two or more vectors.
explanation_steps: A **resultant vector** is the combination of two or more single vectors. When multiple forces or velocities act on an object, the resultant represents the net effect.

questions.stem: The area under the velocity - time graph gives_____________.
explanation_steps: In a velocity-time ($$ v-t $$) graph, the **area** between the plot and the time axis represents the **displacement** of the object. If the area is above the axis, displacement is positive; if below, it is negative.

questions.stem: ______________ is produced by excitation of gaseous atom.
explanation_steps: When atoms in a gas are excited (e.g., by heat or electricity), electrons jump to higher energy levels. When they fall back, they emit light at specific wavelengths, creating a **line emission spectrum**.

questions.stem: The force which opposes the motion of an object is called _________.
explanation_steps: **Friction** is a force that acts between two surfaces in contact and always acts in the direction opposite to the intended or actual motion.
